text:
Rina: FYI rack-12/us-west-2 showing a strange egress jitter pattern since 02:10 UTC. P95 for short gens jumped ~120ms and we see repeated preemptions from fractional-dedicated slices.
Matt: saw the alert. Are NVLINK counters correlated or is this pure NIC egress?
Rina: both. NVLINK TX/RX counters spike right before NIC TX burst. Looks like a mixed IO storm.
Hao: any recent deploys or batch windows hitting that rack?
Rina: nightly best-effort batch started at 02:00 and several jobs landed on hosts in rack-12.
Jules: could be those jobs saturating host PCIe/NVLINK and causing upstream NIC queueing, which cascades to preemption choke.
Matt: if it's PCIe+nvlink, simple NIC shaping won't fully help. We can try host-level eBPF qdisc to limit batch job egress immediately while we investigate. Low risk rollback.
Hao: agree. Proposed emergency: apply eBPF packet-shaping to best-effort cgroup on hosts in rack-12, throttle to 40% egress, and mark tenants >150qps to warm-pool routing for 30m. Canary the routing change to 10% traffic first.
Rina: +1. Can we get metrics for "nic_tx_qdepth" and "nvlink_bandwidth_util" annotated in the preemptions dashboard? want side-by-side.
Jules: I'll add panels. Also add an alert on nvlink > 85% for 2 minutes.
Matt: steps I'm taking now:
1) push eBPF limiter to rack-12 hosts (best-effort cgroup)
2) flip allocator routing label for warm-pool preference (canary 10%)
3) monitor requeue_rate, p95, nic_tx_qdepth, nvlink_util for 20 minutes
4) rollback if tenant SLA drop > 2% or error rate rises

Matt: eBPF command (deploying via fleet-ops):
```
fleetctl run --hosts rack-12 --cmd "ebpf-qos --cgroup best-effort --egress 40% --tag incident-1829990000"
```
oncall-bot: eBPF QoS run scheduled on 6 hosts in rack-12.
Hao: allocator patch for warm-pool canary (10%):
```
kubectl patch configmap allocator-policy -n fleet --type merge -p '{"data":{"warm_pool_canary":"0.10"}}'
```
Rina: linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/noise/egress-jitter and https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/allocs/warmpool-canary
Jules: added nvlink alert rule id=nvlink-high-85. will mute for 2m while we deploy to avoid noise.
Matt: eBPF limiter applied. Initial telemetry shows nic_tx_qdepth down ~30% in the affected hosts within 45s. nvlink_util dropped ~25% after 90s.
Rina: good. Preemptions count also down, but still some requeues into the rack. How is allocator responding to the routing canary?
Hao: canary at 10% is active. requeue_same_rack_count metric decreased by ~35% in first 8m. p95 improved ~60ms.
Jules: still seeing a few tenants with persistent small tail regressions, likely stateful workloads that rehydrate KV caches when moved. We should track tenant IDs and avoid moving them until warm-pool has warmed.
Matt: adding a temporary sticky label for those tenants to avoid warm-pool switches. Will annotate which tenant IDs in the incident doc.
Rina: ops note: keep eBPF limiter on for 30 minutes and review. If stable, we can remove limiter and instead roll a permanent NIC shaping profile or adjust batch scheduler to prefer other racks.
Hao: long-term action item: evaluate host-level PCIe and nvlink visibility, and add allocator heuristic to deprioritize hosts with recent nvlink spikes for 1 hour.
Jules: opening ticket INF-3982 for the allocator heuristic + INF-3983 for batch scheduler affinity tweaks.
oncall-bot: Incident play recorded: "egress-jitter-rack12-ebpf-throttle" at 1829990052
Matt: timeline: eBPF applied at 02:12, canary routing at 02:13, monitoring window 20m -> will reassess at 02:33.
Rina: thanks. if we see error-rate growth or latency for pinned tenants > 2% I'll kill the canary.
Hao: noting that disabling eBPF quickly restored throughput on a test host earlier; so it's safe to revert if needed.
Jules: I'm writing a short runbook section for this: how to target best-effort batches by cgroup, apply eBPF limiter, and how to annotate allocator canary flips. Will link in ticket.
Rina: summary so far: mitigation applied, early signal looks positive (nvlink and nic qdepth down, requeues reduced). Continue monitoring -> decide 02:33 to either expand warm-pool to 50% or dial batch scheduler away from rack-12.
Matt: will update here at 02:33. thanks team.
